title: Priority-probation thawer: adaptive probation slots to reduce starvation in continuous batcher
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: under steady-state continuous-batching workloads we observed long-tail starvation of low-priority ticket groups when high-throughput KV-heavy requests held slots indefinitely. This PR introduces an adaptive "probation thawer" that temporarily promotes a small number of probation slots for starving lanes and uses a timed thaw-and-evaluate window to re-balance fairness without harming overall throughput. Changes include: adaptive probation counters per queue, time-sliced thaw windows with randomized jitter to avoid synchronization, soft-priority decay to prevent permanent promotions, and a KV-prefetch hint integration so thawed slots can warm KV pins when applicable. The description below is a single continuous string containing context, checklist, testing notes and rollout plan. Implementation summary: - add probation state machine to queue metadata (probation_enter_ts, probation_votes) - coordinator exposes a new throttle_sample endpoint used by the autoscaler to get probation pressure metrics - thaw windows are small (default 15ms) and capped per-cohort to limit tail amplification - probation promotions expire after N successful completions or T ms without improvement (configurable) - KV-prefetch hints are added to the scheduler handoff path so thawed requests can request KV warmups before kernel dispatch. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-3274) - [x] deterministic unit tests for state transitions - [x] integration tests in local perf-lab harness - [x] load tests against cohort mix (low-priority background + high-priority serving) - [x] docs and config defaults updated Rollout plan: start with canary in dedicated cluster region, monitor p95/p99 latency for low-priority lanes and overall throughput, enable auto-disable if global tail increases by >7%. Related work: builds on earlier admission/backoff changes (refs: ENG-2103) and KV-pin warmup experiments.

release_notes: Introduces an adaptive 'probation thawer' scheduler mechanism that reduces starvation of low-priority queues under continuous batching. Improves fairness for background lanes with minimal impact to high-priority throughput. Configurable via configs/defaults.yaml; disabled by default for existing clusters. See docs/ops/probation-thawer.md for operational guidance.
performance_results: Experiment mix: 70% high-priority KV-heavy, 30% low-priority background
Low-priority p95 latency: reduced from 420ms to 85ms (canary, median of 5 runs)
System overall throughput: -0.8% on token/sec compared to baseline (within safety window)
Tail safety: global p99 unchanged within 1.5% (monitoring threshold)
KV warmup hit-rate on thawed slots: +32% (reduced cold-pin misses)
notes_for_ops: Default config keeps probation disabled; enable via probation.enabled=true for canaries
Emergency rollback: set probation.enabled=false and restart coordinator process - change is guarded to be safe to toggle at runtime
Suggested initial thresholds: thaw_window_ms=15, probation_max_promotions=3, thaw_cohort_cap=2
